title: Personal Ops + Telegram Bot
tagline: Personal agenda with a local-LLM conversation bot
problem: Organizing my personal routine and university handball training planning in one place — with proactive reminders and conversational control through Telegram, without paying for an LLM API or sending personal data to third parties.
targetUser: Myself (single user, authenticated, server bound to localhost only).
process: Single Flask server for site + REST API; no-build frontend (plain HTML/CSS/JS, Tailwind and FullCalendar via CDN); data in plain JSON — deliberately no database. Telegram conversation bot backed by a local model (Ollama): free-form questions about the agenda, create/edit/complete/delete for tasks and events, batch actions — always with explicit confirmation before writing. Automatic notifications with periodic summaries and an independent watchdog that pings me if the server goes down.
keyDecisions: Radical simplicity: Flask + JSON + CDN — zero build, zero infra; the app starts from a .bat in Windows Startup.
Every conversation-triggered write asks "yes/no" before saving — batch actions included (the real item list is shown before confirming).
When information is missing (event location, actual completion date), the bot asks instead of assuming.
Dual auth: browser session for the UI, Bearer token for automation.
Anti-hallucination in code, not in the prompt: model-generated notifications are only accepted if they mention every real item title; otherwise it falls back to deterministic text.
result: In daily use: full CRUD via web and via conversation, periodic summaries until an "end the day" command, actual-completion date separate from the deadline, date-grouped UI with a completed section, and a watchdog reporting server down/up.
learned: Local models hallucinate even with an explicit "never invent" instruction — the protection that works is validating output in code against real data, with a deterministic fallback. And the simplest possible stack (no build, no database) is a feature when the goal is running every day with zero maintenance.
